claim: An August 2025 channel census puts total YouTube channels at approximately 115 million against roughly 60 million uploading in any given month, implying that around half of all channels are dormant at any point in time.
stance_target: The position that channel-level abandonment is the normal outcome and that active-creator counts are roughly half of cumulative channel counts
scope_conditions: Awesome Creator Academy blog, 2 August 2025; NO methodology or data source is disclosed anywhere in the post, numbers are presumably scraped from a third-party channel database; 'monthly active channels uploading' is not defined; dormancy in a single month is a weak proxy for permanent attrition
quoted_support: That is less than 1% of all the YouTube Channels World Wide (115M YouTube Channels, over 60M monthly active channels uploading each month).

claim: As of August 2025, 618,955 YouTube channels globally had 100,000 or more subscribers and 69,182 had one million or more, with 90% of all channels below 1,000 subscribers and 97% below 10,000.
stance_target: The position that the subscriber distribution across creators is extremely concentrated, with career-scale audiences held by well under 1% of channels
scope_conditions: Awesome Creator Academy blog, 2 August 2025; no methodology disclosed; RELIABILITY WARNING: the same bullet list states both '678' and '6' US channels with 10 million or more subscribers in consecutive lines, an internal contradiction indicating the figures are transcribed rather than computed
quoted_support: 618,955 YouTube Channels have over 100,000 Subscribers (or more) in 2025... 90% of all YouTube channels have less than 1000 Subscribers, and 97% of Channels have less than 10,000 Subscribers on YouTube.

claim: Large-audience YouTube channels are concentrated outside the high-CPM West: India leads Play Button awards (100,000+ subscribers) with 144,430, ahead of the United States at 105,960, with Indonesia fourth at 26,647 and Brazil third at 33,835.
stance_target: The assumption that audience-size distributions measured on Western creator populations describe the global creator population, or that audience size and income scale together across countries
scope_conditions: Awesome Creator Academy blog, August 2025; no methodology disclosed; Play Button award counts are a proxy for the 100k+ subscriber tier; directly relevant to the Southeast Asia generalization question because Indonesia ranks fourth globally on audience scale while sitting in the lowest advertising CPM tier
quoted_support: India has the most YouTube Play Buttons (144,430), United States has the second most (105,960), Brazil has the 3rd most (33,835), followed by Indonesia in fourth with (26,647), and Japan in fifth place with (16,368).
region: Global with country breakdown; Indonesia is the only Southeast Asian country listed
